I've been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life. I know this soil like I know my own hands. At 72, I can't do as much by hand as I used to, so I rely on the agricultural machinery cooperative for seeding, spraying, and harvest. My sons are in Handan city. I farm about 8 mu — the rest I've rented out.

Quzhou is wheat-corn country. That's what I grow. Always has been. The rotation makes sense: wheat in winter, corn in summer, same land. I don't experiment with vegetables or cotton anymore — that's too much hand labor. Wheat and corn I can mechanize almost entirely.

I've been to the extension lectures at the county office. I know our groundwater is dropping. I've cut my irrigation to what the crop actually needs. Three waterings for wheat — before winter dormancy, at jointing, at heading. Corn usually gets by on rain here in summer, maybe one irrigation if July is dry.

I use improved seed varieties, not hybrid corn. I know hybrid gives higher yield but I buy from the cooperative's seed supply and the improved varieties they stock have been reliable for my conditions. For wheat I use Jimai series — proven in Hebei.

My nitrogen is lower than my neighbors'. The scientists from the agricultural university came through here years ago and I listened. I apply 15 kg N per mu on wheat split between base and topdress, around 13 on corn. My yields are steady, my costs are lower.

For tillage: rotary on wheat ground after corn harvest to chop the stubble. No-till direct seeding for corn after wheat — saves time, saves soil moisture, and I can't manage deep plowing alone anymore.
